subject: DI01000021

intro_text.en: Unit 3 of Mathematics-I: what a vector is and how it differs from a scalar; magnitude, unit vector and direction cosines; addition by the triangle and parallelogram laws, subtraction and position vectors, and the i j k component form; the scalar product with its properties, the angle between two vectors and projections; the vector product with its determinant form, properties and the area of a parallelogram and a triangle; and the two applications the syllabus names - work done (F · d) and moment of force (r × F). Twenty-six fully solved numericals.

h.en: 1.1 Scalar or vector: the first question

body.en:
Definition

A scalar has size only (mass, time, temperature, work). A vector has size and direction (displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, momentum).

Notation

  • A vector is written a (bold) or with an arrow above it; its magnitude is |a| or a.
  • Geometrically a vector is a directed line segment: length = magnitude, arrow = direction.
  • A vector is unchanged by moving it parallel to itself - only length and direction matter.
  • Equal vectors have the same magnitude and direction; they need not start at the same point.

Worked example

A displacement of 5 m east is a vector; 5 m is its magnitude and east is its direction. Saying "the car went 60 km" describes a scalar, while "60 km north" describes a vector.

h.en: 1.2 Magnitude, unit vector and direction cosines

body.en:
Definition

For a = a₁i + a₂j + a₃k the magnitude is |a| = √(a₁² + a₂² + a₃²) - Pythagoras in three dimensions. The unit vector a-hat = a/|a| has length 1 and points the same way.

Direction cosines

The angles α, β, γ that a makes with the x, y and z axes have cosines cos α = a₁/|a|, cos β = a₂/|a|, cos γ = a₃/|a|, and cos²α + cos²β + cos²γ = 1.

Worked example

For a = 2i + 3j − 6k: |a| = √(4 + 9 + 36) = 7, so a-hat = (2i + 3j − 6k)/7 and the direction cosines are 2/7, 3/7, −6/7. Check: (4 + 9 + 36)/49 = 1 ✓.

Common mistake / conditions

Divide every component by the same magnitude. A unit vector must come out with length 1 - square its components as a check before moving on.

h.en: 1.3 Types of vectors you will meet

body.en:
The vocabulary

NameMeaningExample
Zero (null)magnitude 0, no directiona − a = 0
Unitmagnitude exactly 1i, j, k
Equalsame magnitude and directionAB and CD in a parallelogram
Negative of asame length, opposite direction−a
Collinearparallel, so one is a scalar multiple of the other2i + 4j and i + 2j
Coplanarall lie in one planeany three vectors with zero scalar triple product

Why the vocabulary matters

Two vectors are parallel exactly when their cross product is zero, and perpendicular exactly when their dot product is zero. Those two sentences answer a large share of the paper.

h.en: 2.1 Addition: triangle and parallelogram laws

body.en:
Definition

Triangle law: place the tail of b at the head of a; then a + b runs from the tail of a to the head of b. Parallelogram law: if a and b are adjacent sides, a + b is the diagonal through the common point.

Properties

  • Commutative: a + b = b + a.
  • Associative: (a + b) + c = a + (b + c).
  • Zero vector: a + 0 = a.
  • Addition is done component by component in i, j, k form.

Worked example

a = 2i + 3j − k and b = i − 2j + 4k give a + b = 3i + j + 3k and |a + b| = √(9 + 1 + 9) = √19 ≈ 4.36.

Common mistake / conditions

Magnitudes do not add like numbers: |a + b| = 4.36 while |a| + |b| = 3.74 + 4.58 = 8.32. The triangle inequality only promises |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|.

h.en: 2.2 Subtraction and position vectors

body.en:
Definition

a − b = a + (−b): reverse b, then add. In components subtract directly. The vector from point A to point B is AB = OB − OA (head minus tail).

Worked examples

With the vectors above, a − b = i + 5j − 5k, of magnitude √51 ≈ 7.14.

For A(1, 2, 3) and B(4, 6, 3): AB = (4 − 1)i + (6 − 2)j + (3 − 3)k = 3i + 4j + 0k, so |AB| = 5 - the distance formula in three dimensions.

Common mistake / conditions

Subtract in the order head minus tail. AB and BA are negatives of each other; choosing the wrong order flips every sign and usually the final answer's sign too.

h.en: 2.3 Components, i j k form and scalar multiplication

body.en:
Definition

i, j, k are unit vectors along x, y, z. Any vector is a = a₁i + a₂j + a₃k, where the components are the projections on the three axes.

Rules

OperationRuleExample
Scalar multiplek(a₁i + a₂j + a₃k) = ka₁i + ka₂j + ka₃k3(2i − j) = 6i − 3j
Additionadd matching components(2i + j) + (i + 4j) = 3i + 5j
Magnitude√(a₁² + a₂² + a₃²)|3i + 4j| = 5
Parallel testb = k a for some scalar k(2, 4) = 2(1, 2)

Worked example

If a = i − 2j + 3k and b = 2i + j − k, then 2a − 3b = (2 − 6)i + (−4 − 3)j + (6 + 3)k = −4i − 7j + 9k, of magnitude √(16 + 49 + 81) = √146 ≈ 12.08.

h.en: 3.1 Definition and properties

body.en:
Definition

a · b = |a||b| cos θ, where θ is the angle between the vectors (0° to 180°). The answer is a scalar - a number, not a vector.

In components

a · b = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃. Multiply matching components and add: this is why the dot product is easy in i, j, k form.

Properties

  • Commutative: a · b = b · a.
  • Distributive: a · (b + c) = a · b + a · c.
  • a · a = |a|², so |a| = √(a · a).
  • i · i = j · j = k · k = 1 and i · j = j · k = k · i = 0.
  • a · b = 0 ⇔ a and b are perpendicular (or one is zero).

Worked example

(i + 2j + 3k) · (4i − 5j + 6k) = 4 − 10 + 18 = 12.

h.en: 3.2 Angle between two vectors

body.en:
Formula

cos θ = (a · b)/(|a||b|), so θ = cos⁻¹ of that value. The formula is just the definition rearranged.

Procedure

  1. Compute a · b in components.
  2. Compute |a| and |b| separately.
  3. Divide, then take the inverse cosine - keep the answer in degrees or radians as asked.

Worked example

a = 2i − j + k and b = i + j + 2k: a · b = 2 − 1 + 2 = 3, |a| = |b| = √6, so cos θ = 3/6 = 1/2 and θ = 60°.

Common mistake / conditions

If cos θ comes out negative, θ is obtuse - do not "fix" the sign. A zero dot product means 90°, and cos⁻¹(1) = 0° means the vectors are parallel in the same direction.

h.en: 3.3 Projection and the perpendicularity condition

body.en:
Definition

The scalar projection of a on b is the length of a's shadow along b: (a · b)/|b|. The vector projection is that length times the unit vector b-hat.

Geometry

In a · b = |a||b| cos θ, the factor |a| cos θ is exactly the projection of a on b. That is why work is F · d: only the component of force along the displacement does work.

Worked example

Projection of a = 3i + j − 2k on b = i + j + k: a · b = 3 + 1 − 2 = 2 and |b| = √3, so the projection is 2/√3 ≈ 1.155.

Finding an unknown

If 2i + λj + k must be perpendicular to i − 2j + 3k, set the dot product to zero: 2 − 2λ + 3 = 0, so λ = 5/2. One equation, one unknown - always the same pattern.

h.en: 4.1 Definition and the determinant form

body.en:
Definition

a × b = |a||b| sin θ n-hat, where n-hat is the unit vector perpendicular to both, given by the right-hand rule. The answer is a vector.

Determinant form

a × b = |i j k; a₁ a₂ a₃; b₁ b₂ b₃| = i(a₂b₃ − a₃b₂) − j(a₁b₃ − a₃b₁) + k(a₁b₂ − a₂b₁).

Worked example

a = 2i + j + 3k, b = i − 2j + k: expanding the determinant gives (1 + 6)i − (2 − 3)j + (−4 − 1)k = 7i + j − 5k, of magnitude √75 = 5√3 ≈ 8.66.

Common mistake / conditions

The middle term carries a minus. Writing +j(...) instead of −j(...) is the single most common error in this question; check by taking a × a, which must be 0.

h.en: 4.2 Properties of the cross product

body.en:
Properties

PropertyStatementConsequence
Anti-commutativea × b = −(b × a)order matters - unlike the dot product
Zero for parallela × a = 0parallel vectors give a zero cross product
Distributivea × (b + c) = a × b + a × cexpand and collect
Scalar(ka) × b = k(a × b)pull constants out
Basisi × j = k, j × k = i, k × i = jcyclic order, anticlockwise

Right-hand rule

Curl the fingers of the right hand from a to b; the thumb points along a × b. Reversing the order reverses the thumb, which is the anti-commutative property in physical form.

Magnitude as an area

|a × b| = |a||b| sin θ is the area of the parallelogram with sides a and b, because the height is |b| sin θ. This is the fastest way to compute areas in three dimensions.

h.en: 4.3 Area of a parallelogram and a triangle

body.en:
Formulae

Parallelogram: area = |a × b| for adjacent sides a and b.

Triangle: area = ½|a × b|, because a triangle is half of the parallelogram.

Three vertices

With A, B, C given, take a = AB = B − A and b = AC = C − A, then area = ½|a × b|. Starting from one vertex matters - using two different starting points gives the wrong vectors.

Worked example

A(1, 1, 1), B(2, 3, 4), C(4, 2, 3): AB = i + 2j + 3k, AC = 3i + j + 2k, and AB × AC = i(4 − 3) − j(2 − 9) + k(1 − 6) = i + 7j − 5k. |a × b| = √75 = 5√3, so the area is 5√3/2 ≈ 4.33 square units.

Collinearity

Three points are collinear exactly when a × b = 0. That is the 3-D version of the determinant test from Unit 1.

title.en: 5. Applications: Work Done and Moment of Force

h.en: 5.1 Work done by a force

body.en:
Definition

W = F · d = |F||d| cos θ, where θ is the angle between the force and the displacement. Work is a scalar measured in joules (N·m).

Why the dot product

Only the component of the force along the motion contributes. If F is perpendicular to d (carrying a bag horizontally), cos 90° = 0 and no work is done - which matches everyday experience and the formula.

Worked example

F = 3i + 2j − k newton moves an object through d = 2i − j + 3k metre. W = 6 − 2 − 3 = 1 J. A small positive value means the force mostly pushes sideways.

Conditions

Use the displacement, not the distance travelled; and keep the units consistent (N and m give J). A negative dot product means the force opposes the motion.

h.en: 5.2 Moment of a force about a point

body.en:
Definition

M = r × F, where r is the position vector of the point of application measured from the point about which the moment is taken. The moment is a vector, in N·m, and its direction gives the axis of rotation.

Magnitude

|M| = |r||F| sin θ = F × (perpendicular distance). Both forms appear in exams; the second is faster when the perpendicular distance is given directly.

Worked example

r = 3i − j + 2k and F = 2i + j − k give M = r × F = |i j k; 3 −1 2; 2 1 −1| = −i + 7j + 5k, of magnitude √75 = 5√3 ≈ 8.66 N·m.

Common mistake / conditions

Take r from the correct point. A moment "about A" needs r = position of the force minus position of A, not the position of the force from the origin.

h.en: 5.3 Choosing dot or cross: a decision guide

body.en:
The question behind every problem

Question wordingProductBecause
"Find the angle between"dotcos θ comes from a · b
"Work done by the force"dotW = F · d is a scalar
"Show the vectors are perpendicular"dota · b = 0
"Find the area / a perpendicular vector"cross|a × b| is an area
"Moment of the force"crossM = r × F is a vector
"Show the vectors are parallel"crossa × b = 0

Mixed-problem routine

  1. Write both vectors in i, j, k form.
  2. Decide dot or cross from the table above.
  3. Compute carefully, keeping the minus in the cross product's middle term.
  4. State units and the geometric meaning of the answer.

Check worth doing

For any pair, |a × b|² + (a · b)² = |a|²|b|². Testing this on your numbers catches almost every arithmetic slip before it costs marks.

h.en: Practice 1. Find the magnitude and unit vector of a = 6i + 2j − 3k.

body.en:
Working

  1. |a| = √(36 + 4 + 9) = √49 = 7
  2. a-hat = (6i + 2j − 3k)/7

Answer

7 and (6i + 2j − 3k)/7. Check the unit vector's length: (36 + 4 + 9)/49 = 1 ✓.

h.en: Practice 2. For a = i + j and b = i − j, find a · b and the angle between them.

body.en:
Working

  1. a · b = 1 − 1 = 0
  2. |a| = |b| = √2
  3. cos θ = 0, so θ = 90°

Check

A zero dot product is the perpendicularity test, so 90° must be the answer - the two vectors are the diagonals of a square.

h.en: Practice 3. Find the angle between i + 2j + 2k and 2i + j − 2k.

body.en:
Working

  1. a · b = 2 + 2 − 4 = 0
  2. Both magnitudes are 3
  3. cos θ = 0, so θ = 90°

Answer

90°. Since the dot product vanished, the vectors are perpendicular; there is no need to compute the magnitudes at all, but they confirm the result is not a division by zero.

h.en: Practice 4. Find a × b for a = 3i − j + 2k and b = i + 2j − k.
Practice 5. Find the area of the parallelogram with sides i + 2j + 3k and 2i + j + k.

body.en:
Working

  1. a × b = i(2 − 3) − j(1 − 6) + k(1 − 4) = −i + 5j − 3k
  2. |a × b| = √(1 + 25 + 9) = √35 ≈ 5.92

Answer

√35 ≈ 5.92 square units. The area must be less than |a||b| = 3.74 × 2.45 = 9.17, and it is ✓.

h.en: Practice 6. Find λ so that 3i + λj − 2k is perpendicular to 2i − j + 4k.

body.en:
Working

  1. Perpendicular means a · b = 0
  2. 3(2) + λ(−1) + (−2)(4) = 0
  3. 6 − λ − 8 = 0
  4. λ = −2

Answer

λ = −2. Check: 6 + 2 − 8 = 0 ✓. One equation, one unknown - this "perpendicularity gives the unknown" pattern is worth recognising instantly.

h.en: Practice 7. Find the work done by F = 4i − j + 2k along d = 2i + 3j − k.

body.en:
Working

W = 8 − 3 − 2 = 3 J.

Answer

3 J. Positive work means the force has a component along the displacement; the j-components partially cancel.

h.en: Practice 8. Find the moment of F = 3i + j acting at r = 2i − j about the origin.

body.en:
Working

  1. M = |i j k; 2 −1 0; 3 1 0|
  2. = i(0) − j(0) + k(2 + 3) = 5k

Answer

5k N·m, magnitude 5. The moment is about the z-axis because everything lies in the xy-plane; check M · r = 0 ✓.

h.en: Practice 9. Find the projection of 2i + 3j − k on i + j + k.

body.en:
Working

  1. a · b = 2 + 3 − 1 = 4
  2. |b| = √3
  3. projection = 4/√3 ≈ 2.31

Answer

4/√3 ≈ 2.31. Rationalised: 4√3/3. The projection is smaller than |a| = √14 ≈ 3.74 ✓.

h.en: Practice 10. Show that the points A(1, 2, 3), B(2, 3, 4) and C(3, 4, 5) are collinear.

body.en:
Working

  1. AB = i + j + k
  2. AC = 2i + 2j + 2k = 2AB
  3. Since AC is a scalar multiple of AB, the cross product is zero

Answer

Collinear. The points lie on the line through (1, 2, 3) with direction i + j + k, which is x − 1 = y − 2 = z − 3.

h.en: Practice 11. If |a| = 5, |b| = 12 and a · b = 30, find the angle between a and b.
Practice 12. Find a vector of magnitude 6 perpendicular to both i + j and i − j.

body.en:
Working

  1. (i + j) × (i − j) = i(0) − j(0) + k(−1 − 1) = −2k
  2. Unit perpendicular = ±k
  3. Required vector = ±6k

Answer

±6k. Both given vectors lie in the xy-plane, so any perpendicular is along z - the answer must have no i or j component.

h.en: Practice 13. Find the moment of F = 2i + 3j + k acting at A(1, 1, 1) about B(0, 1, 1).

body.en:
Working

  1. r = OA − OB = i + 0j + 0k
  2. M = |i j k; 1 0 0; 2 3 1| = i(0) − j(1) + k(3) = −j + 3k

Answer

−j + 3k N·m, magnitude √10 ≈ 3.16. The arm has no y or z component, so only two terms survive - subtract the right point to keep it that way.

h.en: Practice 14. Find the area of the triangle with vertices (0, 0, 0), (2, 1, 0) and (1, 3, 4).

body.en:
Working

  1. a = 2i + j, b = i + 3j + 4k
  2. a × b = i(4 − 0) − j(8 − 0) + k(6 − 1) = 4i − 8j + 5k
  3. |a × b| = √(16 + 64 + 25) = √105
  4. area = √105/2 ≈ 5.12

Answer

√105/2 ≈ 5.12 square units. Half the parallelogram area is expected, since the triangle is exactly half of it.

h.en: Practice 15. A force F = 2i − j + 3k acts at the point P(1, 2, 3). Find its moment about Q(2, 0, 1) and the work done if the point moves from P to Q.

body.en:
Working

  1. r = OP − OQ = −i + 2j + 2k
  2. M = |i j k; −1 2 2; 2 −1 3| = i(6 + 2) − j(−3 − 4) + k(1 − 4) = 8i + 7j − 3k
  3. d = OQ − OP = i − 2j − 2k, so W = 2 − (−2) + (−6) = −2 J

Answer

M = 8i + 7j − 3k (|M| = √122 ≈ 11.05 N·m); W = −2 J. Negative work means the force opposes that displacement - consistent with the moment's large magnitude.

q.en: Find the magnitude of a = 3i − 4j + 12k.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Three components, one negative.

Formula

|a| = √(a₁² + a₂² + a₃²)

Step-by-step solution

  1. 3² = 9, (−4)² = 16, 12² = 144
  2. Sum = 169
  3. |a| = √169 = 13

Interpretation and check

13 units. The 3-4-12 triple always gives 13 - worth remembering, like 3-4-5 in two dimensions.

q.en: Write the unit vector along a = 2i + 3j − 6k.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

First find the magnitude, then divide every component by it.

Formula

a-hat = a/|a|

Step-by-step solution

  1. |a| = √(4 + 9 + 36) = √49 = 7
  2. a-hat = (2i + 3j − 6k)/7

Interpretation and check

(2/7)i + (3/7)j − (6/7)k. Check the length: (4 + 9 + 36)/49 = 1 ✓. A unit vector is the fastest way to answer "find a vector of magnitude 10 in this direction" - multiply a-hat by 10.

q.en: Find the direction cosines of a = i + 2j + 2k.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Direction cosines are the components divided by the magnitude.

Formula

cos α = a₁/|a|, cos β = a₂/|a|, cos γ = a₃/|a|

Step-by-step solution

  1. |a| = √(1 + 4 + 4) = 3
  2. cos α = 1/3, cos β = 2/3, cos γ = 2/3
  3. α ≈ 70.5°, β ≈ 48.2°, γ ≈ 48.2°

Interpretation and check

1/3, 2/3, 2/3. Check the identity: (1 + 4 + 4)/9 = 1 ✓. All three angles are between 0° and 180°, as direction angles must be.

q.en: For a = 2i + 3j − k and b = i − 2j + 4k find a + b, a − b and their magnitudes.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Add and subtract component by component.

Formula

(a₁ ± b₁)i + (a₂ ± b₂)j + (a₃ ± b₃)k

Step-by-step solution

  1. a + b = 3i + j + 3k
  2. |a + b| = √(9 + 1 + 9) = √19 ≈ 4.36
  3. a − b = i + 5j − 5k
  4. |a − b| = √(1 + 25 + 25) = √51 ≈ 7.14

Interpretation and check

√19 ≈ 4.36 and √51 ≈ 7.14. Note that |a| + |b| = 3.74 + 4.58 = 8.32 is larger than both, so the triangle inequality holds but magnitudes do not add directly.

q.en: Find the angle between a = 2i − j + k and b = i + j + 2k.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Dot product and both magnitudes.

Formula

cos θ = (a · b)/(|a||b|)

Step-by-step solution

  1. a · b = 2 − 1 + 2 = 3
  2. |a| = √6 and |b| = √6
  3. cos θ = 3/6 = 1/2
  4. θ = 60°

Interpretation and check

60°. The symmetry (|a| = |b|) is a hint: equal lengths often give a standard angle. A positive cosine confirms the angle is acute.

q.en: Find the dot product of p = i + 2j + 3k and q = 4i − 5j + 6k.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Multiply matching components and add.

Formula

p · q = p₁q₁ + p₂q₂ + p₃q₃

Step-by-step solution

  1. 1 × 4 = 4
  2. 2 × (−5) = −10
  3. 3 × 6 = 18
  4. 4 − 10 + 18 = 12

Interpretation and check

12. A positive dot product means the angle between them is acute. Since the vectors are nowhere near parallel (their components differ a lot), a moderate positive value is expected.

q.en: Find the angle between 2i + 2j − k and 6i − 3j + 2k.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Both magnitudes are Pythagorean, which keeps the arithmetic exact.

Formula

cos θ = (a · b)/(|a||b|)

Step-by-step solution

  1. a · b = 12 − 6 − 2 = 4
  2. |a| = √9 = 3, |b| = √49 = 7
  3. cos θ = 4/21 ≈ 0.1905
  4. θ ≈ 79.0°

Interpretation and check

θ ≈ 79°. A small positive cosine means an angle just under 90°, so the vectors are nearly - but not quite - perpendicular. Check with |a × b|: √(441 − 16) = √425 ≈ 20.6, so sin θ = 20.6/21 ≈ 0.98 ✓.

q.en: Find λ so that 2i + λj + k is perpendicular to i − 2j + 3k.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Perpendicular means the dot product is zero.

Formula

a · b = 0

Step-by-step solution

  1. 2(1) + λ(−2) + 1(3) = 0
  2. 5 − 2λ = 0
  3. λ = 5/2

Interpretation and check

λ = 2.5. Check: 2 − 5 + 3 = 0 ✓. This "find the unknown from perpendicularity" pattern appears in almost every paper.

q.en: Find the projection of a = 3i + j − 2k on b = i + j + k.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Projection means the shadow length of a along b.

Formula

projection = (a · b)/|b|

Step-by-step solution

  1. a · b = 3 + 1 − 2 = 2
  2. |b| = √3
  3. projection = 2/√3 ≈ 1.155

Interpretation and check

2/√3 ≈ 1.15. Rationalising gives 2√3/3. The projection is shorter than |a| = √14 ≈ 3.74, as it must be for any non-zero angle.

q.en: Find a × b for a = 2i + j + 3k and b = i − 2j + k.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Expand the determinant, keeping the minus on the j-term.

Formula

a × b = |i j k; 2 1 3; 1 −2 1|

Step-by-step solution

  1. i(1×1 − 3×(−2)) = i(1 + 6) = 7i
  2. −j(2×1 − 3×1) = −j(2 − 3) = +j
  3. k(2×(−2) − 1×1) = k(−4 − 1) = −5k
  4. a × b = 7i + j − 5k

Interpretation and check

7i + j − 5k. Two checks: dot the answer with a and with b - both must be zero (7(2) + 1(1) − 5(3) = 0 ✓, 7 − 2 − 5 = 0 ✓), which proves it is perpendicular to both.

q.en: Find the area of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are a = 2i + j + 3k and b = i − 2j + k.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Adjacent sides - so the cross product gives the area directly.

Formula

area = |a × b|

Step-by-step solution

  1. a × b = 7i + j − 5k
  2. |a × b| = √(49 + 1 + 25) = √75
  3. = 5√3 ≈ 8.66

Interpretation and check

5√3 ≈ 8.66 square units. A parallelogram area can exceed the product of the side lengths only if the angle is right - here |a||b| = 3.74 × 2.45 = 9.17, slightly more than 8.66, so the angle is not 90° ✓.

q.en: Find the area of the triangle with vertices A(1, 1, 1), B(2, 3, 4) and C(4, 2, 3).

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Take both vectors from the same vertex A.

Formula

area = ½|AB × AC|

Step-by-step solution

  1. AB = i + 2j + 3k and AC = 3i + j + 2k
  2. AB × AC = i(4 − 3) − j(2 − 9) + k(1 − 6) = i + 7j − 5k
  3. |AB × AC| = √(1 + 49 + 25) = √75 = 5√3
  4. area = 5√3/2 ≈ 4.33

Interpretation and check

5√3/2 ≈ 4.33 square units. The triangle is exactly half of the parallelogram on the same two sides - which is where the ½ comes from, not a coincidence.

q.en: Find a unit vector perpendicular to both i + j and j + k.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

A vector perpendicular to both is their cross product.

Formula

n = ±(a × b)/|a × b|

Step-by-step solution

  1. a × b = |i j k; 1 1 0; 0 1 1| = i(1 − 0) − j(1 − 0) + k(1 − 0) = i − j + k
  2. |a × b| = √3
  3. n = ±(i − j + k)/√3

Interpretation and check

±(i − j + k)/√3. Two answers exist because "perpendicular to both" leaves the direction up or down. Check: (1 − 1 + 0)/√3 = 0 and (0 − 1 + 1)/√3 = 0 ✓.

q.en: Find the work done by F = 3i + 2j − k when the displacement is d = 2i − j + 3k.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Force and displacement in newton and metre.

Formula

W = F · d

Step-by-step solution

  1. 3(2) = 6
  2. 2(−1) = −2
  3. (−1)(3) = −3
  4. W = 6 − 2 − 3 = 1 J

Interpretation and check

1 joule. The small positive value means the force is partly along the motion and partly sideways. If the answer had been negative, the force would be retarding.

q.en: A force of 20 N acts at 60° to a displacement of 5 m. Find the work done.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Magnitudes and the angle between them.

Formula

W = |F||d| cos θ

Step-by-step solution

  1. W = 20 × 5 × cos 60°
  2. = 100 × 0.5
  3. = 50 J

Interpretation and check

50 J. At 0° the work would be 100 J and at 90° it would be 0 J; 50 J sits exactly between, as cos 60° = 0.5 predicts.

q.en: Find the moment of F = 2i + j − k acting at r = 3i − j + 2k about the origin.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Moment about O is M = r × F.

Formula

M = |i j k; 3 −1 2; 2 1 −1|

Step-by-step solution

  1. i((−1)(−1) − 2(1)) = i(1 − 2) = −i
  2. −j(3(−1) − 2(2)) = −j(−3 − 4) = 7j
  3. k(3(1) − (−1)(2)) = k(3 + 2) = 5k
  4. M = −i + 7j + 5k

Interpretation and check

−i + 7j + 5k, magnitude √75 = 5√3 ≈ 8.66 N·m. Check M · r = −3 − 7 + 10 = 0 and M · F = −2 + 7 − 5 = 0 ✓ - a moment is perpendicular to both r and F.

q.en: Find the moment of F = i + 2j acting at B(3, 4, 0) about the point A(1, 1, 0).

a.en:
Given and assumptions

The moment arm is measured from A, so r = OB − OA.

Formula

M = r × F with r = B − A

Step-by-step solution

  1. r = (3 − 1)i + (4 − 1)j = 2i + 3j
  2. M = |i j k; 2 3 0; 1 2 0|
  3. = i(0) − j(0) + k(4 − 3) = k

Interpretation and check

M = k, magnitude 1 N·m. The moment points along z because both r and F lie in the xy-plane - a rotation about the z-axis. Using OB instead of B − A is the usual error.

q.en: A force of 40 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 0.5 m from a hinge. Find the moment.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Perpendicular distance given, so the scalar form is fastest.

Formula

|M| = F × perpendicular distance

Step-by-step solution

  1. |M| = 40 × 0.5
  2. = 20

Interpretation and check

20 N·m. Same answer as |r × F| with sin θ = 1. Doubling the distance doubles the moment - the reason a longer spanner loosens a bolt more easily.

q.en: If |a + b| = |a − b|, show that a and b are perpendicular.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Square both sides instead of working with roots.

Formula

|a ± b|² = |a|² ± 2a · b + |b|²

Step-by-step solution

  1. |a|² + 2a · b + |b|² = |a|² − 2a · b + |b|²
  2. 4a · b = 0
  3. a · b = 0, so a ⊥ b

Interpretation and check

a · b = 0, therefore perpendicular. Geometrically the two diagonals of the parallelogram are equal exactly when it is a rectangle - the same statement in words.

q.en: If a = i − 2j + 3k and b = 2i + j − k, find |2a − 3b|.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Form the combination first, then take the magnitude.

Formula

k a scales every component

Step-by-step solution

  1. 2a = 2i − 4j + 6k and 3b = 6i + 3j − 3k
  2. 2a − 3b = −4i − 7j + 9k
  3. |2a − 3b| = √(16 + 49 + 81) = √146 ≈ 12.08

Interpretation and check

√146 ≈ 12.08. Estimate first: |2a| ≈ 2(3.74) = 7.5 and |3b| ≈ 3(2.45) = 7.3, so the difference lies between 0.2 and 14.8 - and 12.08 does.

q.en: Find a vector of magnitude 10 in the direction of 3i + 4j.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Find the unit vector, then multiply by the required magnitude.

Formula

required = magnitude × a-hat

Step-by-step solution

  1. |a| = 5
  2. a-hat = (3i + 4j)/5
  3. 10 a-hat = 6i + 8j

Interpretation and check

6i + 8j. Check: √(36 + 64) = 10 ✓. Direction is unchanged because scaling by a positive number does not rotate a vector.

q.en: For A(1, 2, 3) and B(3, 4, 5) find AB, |AB| and the midpoint.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

AB = OB − OA; the midpoint is the average of the coordinates.

Formula

AB = (x₂ − x₁)i + (y₂ − y₁)j + (z₂ − z₁)k

Step-by-step solution

  1. AB = 2i + 2j + 2k
  2. |AB| = √12 = 2√3 ≈ 3.46
  3. midpoint = (2, 3, 4)

Interpretation and check

2i + 2j + 2k, 2√3 ≈ 3.46, midpoint (2, 3, 4). Check the midpoint is halfway: AM = i + j + k with magnitude √3 = half of 2√3 ✓.

q.en: If a · b = 6, |a| = 3 and |b| = 4, find the angle between a and b.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

All three quantities in the dot-product definition are known except θ.

Formula

cos θ = (a · b)/(|a||b|)

Step-by-step solution

  1. cos θ = 6/(3 × 4) = 6/12
  2. cos θ = 0.5
  3. θ = 60°

Interpretation and check

60°. Since a · b is positive and smaller than |a||b| = 12, the angle must be between 0° and 90° - 60° fits.

q.en: Find the work done by F = i + j + k along the displacement from (1, 2, 3) to (4, 6, 3).

a.en:
Given and assumptions

The displacement vector is the difference of the points.

Formula

W = F · d, with d = B − A

Step-by-step solution

  1. d = 3i + 4j + 0k
  2. W = 1(3) + 1(4) + 1(0)
  3. W = 7 J

Interpretation and check

7 J. The z-component contributes nothing because the displacement has no z-part - only the component of force along the motion does work.

q.en: Find the magnitude of the moment of F = i − j + 2k acting at r = 2i + 3j + k.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Cross product first, then its magnitude.

Formula

M = r × F and |M| = √(M₁² + M₂² + M₃²)

Step-by-step solution

  1. M = i(3×2 − 1×(−1)) − j(2×2 − 1×1) + k(2×(−1) − 3×1)
  2. = i(6 + 1) − j(4 − 1) + k(−2 − 3) = 7i − 3j − 5k
  3. |M| = √(49 + 9 + 25) = √83 ≈ 9.11

Interpretation and check

√83 ≈ 9.11 N·m. Check M · r = 14 − 9 − 5 = 0 ✓ and M · F = 7 + 3 − 10 = 0 ✓, so the moment is perpendicular to both vectors as it must be.

q.en: For |a| = 3, |b| = 4 and a · b = 6, find |a × b| and verify the identity |a × b|² + (a · b)² = |a|²|b|².

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Use the angle from the dot product, then both formulas.

Formula

|a × b| = |a||b| sin θ and sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ

Step-by-step solution

  1. cos θ = 6/12 = 0.5, so sin θ = √3/2
  2. |a × b| = 12 × √3/2 = 6√3 ≈ 10.39
  3. Check: (6√3)² + 6² = 108 + 36 = 144 = 9 × 16 ✓

Interpretation and check

6√3 ≈ 10.39. The identity holds for every pair of vectors, so it doubles as a check on any dot-and-cross question - compute whichever magnitude is easier and derive the other.

q.en: What is the difference between a scalar and a vector?

a.en: A scalar has magnitude only; a vector has magnitude and direction.

q.en: How is the magnitude of a vector found?

a.en: |a| = √(a₁² + a₂² + a₃²), the square root of the sum of squared components.

q.en: What is a unit vector?

a.en: A vector of length 1 in the direction of a, written a/|a|.

q.en: State the triangle law of addition.

a.en: Place the tail of b on the head of a; a + b joins the free tail to the free head.

q.en: How do you find the vector AB from two points?

a.en: AB = OB − OA, that is head minus tail.

q.en: When are two vectors parallel?

a.en: When one is a scalar multiple of the other, equivalently when a × b = 0.

q.en: Define the scalar product.

a.en: a · b = |a||b| cos θ; in components it is a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃.

q.en: What does a · b = 0 mean?

a.en: The vectors are perpendicular (or one of them is the zero vector).

q.en: How is the angle between two vectors found?

a.en: cos θ = (a · b)/(|a||b|), then θ = cos⁻¹ of that value.

q.en: Define the vector product.

a.en: a × b = |a||b| sin θ n-hat, a vector perpendicular to both by the right-hand rule.

q.en: What does a × b = 0 mean?

a.en: The vectors are parallel or antiparallel.

q.en: Is the cross product commutative?

a.en: No: a × b = −(b × a). Only the dot product is commutative.

q.en: What does |a × b| represent geometrically?

a.en: The area of the parallelogram with a and b as adjacent sides.

q.en: State the identity linking dot and cross products.

a.en: |a × b|² + (a · b)² = |a|²|b|².

q.en: Write the formula for work done.

a.en: W = F · d = |F||d| cos θ, measured in joules.

q.en: Why is no work done when the force is perpendicular to the motion?

a.en: Because cos 90° = 0, so only the along-motion component contributes.

q.en: Define the moment of a force.

a.en: M = r × F, a vector in N·m giving the turning effect about a point.

q.en: What is the scalar form of the moment?

a.en: |M| = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot.

q.en: From which point is r measured in M = r × F?

a.en: From the point about which the moment is taken, to the point of application of the force.

q.en: Which product gives the area of a triangle from two vectors?

a.en: Half the magnitude of their cross product, ½|a × b|.

q.en: How do you test three points for collinearity in 3-D?

a.en: Take two vectors from one point; the points are collinear when their cross product is zero.

q.en: Give one practical use of the dot product.

a.en: Finding the work done, or the component of a force along a direction.
